items.title: Explainable machine learning-assisted exploration of chromatin dynamics reveals chromosome-specific response to serum starvation.
items.summary: Journal: eLife. Abstract: Chromatin is dynamic at all length scales, influencing chromatin-based processes, such as gene expression. Even large-scale reorganization of whole chromosome territories has been reported upon specific signals, but the lack of suitable methods has prevented analysis of the underlying dynamic processes. Here, we have used CRISPR-Sirius for time-lapse imaging of chromatin loci dynamics during serum starvation. We show that chromosome 1 loci move toward the nuclear envelope during the first hour of serum starvation in a chromosome-specific manner. Machine learning-assisted exploration of acquired multiparametric data combined with the Shapley values-based explanation approach allowed us to uncover the critical features that characterize chromatin dynamics during serum starvation. This analysis reveals that although serum starvation affects overall nuclear morphology and chromatin dynamics, chromosome 1 loci display a specific response that is characterized by maintenance of dynamics in a constrained environment, and long 'jumps' at the nuclear periphery. Interestingly, the two homologous chromosomes display differential behaviors, with the more peripheral homolog being more responsive to the signal than the internal one. Overall, the presented machine learning-assisted dataset exploration helps us navigate the multidimensional data to understand the underlying dynamic processes and can be applied to a wide variety of research questions in imaging and cell biology in general.
items.headline: Explainable ML reveals chromosome 1-specific chromatin dynamics under serum starvation
items.brief: Using CRISPR-Sirius time-lapse imaging and machine learning with Shapley value explanations, this study uncovers that chromosome 1 loci uniquely move toward the nuclear envelope during serum starvation, maintaining constrained dynamics and exhibiting long jumps at the periphery. This chromosome-specific response contrasts with overall nuclear morphology changes and chromatin dynamics, highlighting differential chromatin reorganization mechanisms.
items.why: It provides a novel explainable ML approach to dissect chromosome-specific chromatin dynamics, advancing understanding of spatial genome regulation under stress.
items.korean: 설명 가능한 머신러닝으로 혈청 결핍 시 염색체 1의 특이적 염색질 역학을 밝혀냈다.

items.title: Evolution of 3D Genome Organization: Mechanisms, Regulation, and Comparative Genomics.
items.summary: Journal: Annual review of animal biosciences. Abstract: How 3D genome architecture varies across species, how it is encoded by molecular mechanisms and genomic sequence, and how it shapes animal evolution are questions that have become tractable only recently. Rapidly expanding chromatin-conformation data sets, chromosome-scale genome assemblies, and advances in computational modeling now enable comparative 3D genomics across broad phylogenetic scales. Here we review recent progress in 3D genome evolution, tracing how chromosome territories, polarized chromosome arrangements, compartments, and topologically associating domains have diversified across lineages. We examine the molecular and sequence determinants of this diversification, including condensin II, CCCTC-binding factor, alternative insulators, repetitive sequences, and large-scale chromosome rearrangements, and consider how architectural change may influence gene regulation, phenotypic divergence, and speciation. Finally, we discuss phylogeny-aware statistical models, sequence-to-contact map predictors, and emerging multimodal foundation models as complementary computational frameworks for identifying conserved and lineage-specific folding patterns, prioritizing sequence changes with predicted architectural effects, and generating testable evolutionary hypotheses.
items.headline: Evolutionary mechanisms and regulation of 3D genome organization across species
items.brief: This review synthesizes recent advances in comparative 3D genomics, detailing how chromosome territories, compartments, and topologically associating domains have diversified across animal lineages. It discusses molecular determinants like condensin II and CTCF, sequence features, and large-scale rearrangements shaping 3D genome architecture, and explores implications for gene regulation, phenotypic divergence, and speciation.
items.why: It integrates evolutionary and mechanistic insights into 3D genome folding, informing computational genomics models of chromatin structure and regulation.
items.korean: 종 간 3D 게놈 구조 진화와 조절 메커니즘을 종합적으로 고찰했다.

items.title: Multi-omics data integration in bioinformatics: methods, applications, and the path toward biological reasoning.
items.summary: Journal: Functional & integrative genomics. Abstract: High-throughput technologies now make it possible to simultaneously generate genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. Spatial and single-cell platforms, in turn, provide cellular and spatial information in greater detail. Relying on a single omics method captures only a fraction of this complexity and often overlooks interactions across different layers. Despite these advances, clinical applications remain limited. This review examines integration strategies, along with their applications in various diseases, and the machine learning methods used to implement them. Rather than focusing solely on predictive performance, the aim is to support biological reasoning by formulating testable hypotheses, drawing causal inferences, and gaining insights that can guide clinical decisions. A reanalysis of a publicly available chronic lymphocytic leukemia dataset revealed that one data type was missing in approximately one-third of patients. When early and intermediate integration were combined with simple zero imputation, agreement dropped to chance and near-chance levels. In contrast, late integration, which does not require data imputation, was largely unaffected by this issue. This demonstrates that findings regarding integration strategies cannot be considered in isolation from how missing data are handled. The review also covers approaches that directly address missing data. Major barriers to clinical application include confounding batch effects, unreliable feature attribution when features are correlated, and deficiencies in clinical quality assurance. This review proposes four criteria to help identify models that not only ensure statistical validity but also genuinely support biological reasoning: mechanistic specificity, causal grounding, failure transparency, and decision relevance.
items.headline: Multi-omics data integration methods for biological reasoning beyond prediction
items.brief: This review covers strategies for integrating genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, emphasizing machine learning methods that support biological reasoning rather than solely predictive accuracy. It highlights challenges like missing data and discusses approaches combining early and intermediate integration to formulate testable hypotheses and causal inferences, demonstrated via reanalysis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia datasets.
items.why: It advances computational genomics by focusing on integrative ML methods that enable mechanistic insights and hypothesis generation from multi-omics data.
items.korean: 생물학적 추론을 위한 다중오믹스 데이터 통합 및 기계학습 방법을 정리했다.
